fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. The writer says they heard it, saw it with their own eyes, gazed upon it and touched it with their own hands (1 John 1:1). That's a front-row seat, and I think he'd have been a little offended by the word secondhand.

Right on, baker. The writer says, “We proclaim to you what we have seen and heard, so that you also may have fellowship with us.” (1 John 1:3). He's opening the door and inviting the readers in. He also says they write so that their joy may be complete (1 John 1:4).

That's right, baker. The writer says, “…if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another…” (1 John 1:7). Walking in the light goes with fellowship, not with losing it. A good kitchen is better when it's full of people.

You've got it, baker. The writer says Jesus “…is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.” (1 John 2:2). That's a big reach, and I can't think of a bigger circle to draw. It doesn't stop with the writer and his readers.
